$comment: GENERATED — do not hand-edit. The route table claudemon actually serves, extracted from the axum routers in services/claudemon/src/daemon/{api,hook}.rs. Regenerate with: make claudemon-routes  (or read the diff a failing services/claudemon `routes_contract` test prints). A hand-maintained copy of this list would drift, which is the disease this fixture exists to cure.
notes: `pattern` is the axum path AS REGISTERED, so `:id` is a wildcard segment and a caller path matches it segment-by-segment with a static segment winning over a wildcard — the same precedence axum applies.

`server` distinguishes the two independent routers on two ports: claudemon-api (:7891, everything a client calls) and claudemon-hook (:7890, ingress for Claude Code's own hook and statusLine shellouts). /health exists on both.
`method` is the axum verb. It is not decoration: /mcp/ask/:session_id is POST-only and axum answers a GET there with 405, so a GET caller is as dead as a caller of a route that does not exist.
owners: services/claudemon/src/daemon/routes_contract.rs (Rust) — extracts the table from the two router sources at compile time and fails if this file disagrees. That is what makes the fixture DERIVED rather than declared.

services/hub/internal/capspec/claudemoncallers_test.go (Go) — sweeps every claudemon HTTP caller in the repo, in three languages, and fails on a path no row here serves; also pins this file to capspec's own httpRoutes registry, which a separate scan already holds to the same two routers.

apps/tui/src/claudemon.rs (Rust) — the TUI's mock_server answers 404 for a path absent from this table and 405 for a method it does not serve, so a client-side route assertion can no longer pin the caller's own URL against itself.
why: 37 routes with no contract is how commit 37320188 deleted claudemon's /git family while apps/tui kept calling six of them for weeks with a green suite. Nothing in the repo compared the paths a caller BUILDS against the paths the daemon SERVES, so the only symptom was a 404 nobody read. The hub bus seam had such a guard (cmd/brain/headless_completeness_test.go) and stayed clean; this seam had none and rotted. This file is the served half of the comparison.
